raw:
Seraphel waits a moment. When you offer no preference, she chooses for herself.

“I’ll start with the clean one and let the tune show;  
The tavern can follow if anyone says so.”

She taps a slow walking rhythm against the table and sings without asking anyone else to join.

“Lanterns low, lanterns low,  
Mark where the late-footed travelers go.

“One for the road and one for the rain;  
Sing at the crossroads and find us again.

“A cooper set out with the moon at his back,  
A loaf in his coat and a song in his pack.

“He followed six lights till the morning sky showed,  
Then found he had walked on the wrong lantern road.”

Her voice is clear but unadorned, suited to a song meant to be carried outdoors. Rashid picks up the rhythm on the table during the repeated chorus. Aldric joins quietly on the second pass, knowing every word. Ashara waits until the clean verse ends.

Then she supplies the tavern version in a low, forceful voice.

“Keep your damned lantern down in the ditch;  
The tollman’s a bastard, the landlord is rich.

“If rain takes your blanket and mud takes your bed,  
Drink deep with the robbers who robbed you instead.”

Caelindra lowers her spoon. “The rhyme is better.”

“The meter is worse,” Aldric says.

“It improves when shouted.”

“You omitted the third obscenity.”

“Dessert hasn’t arrived.”

Seraphel laughs, warm light brightening around her face. You listen without joining the performance, eating while the others carry the chorus around the table. By the time honey cakes arrive, even Caelindra is quietly supplying the final line, though she continues to object to *road* rhyming with *rode*.
reasoning_summaries: **Planning layered song versions and character roles**
